candidate_sentence_map.S1: Heimstaden reported stronger underlying performance in 2025 despite flat headline rental income and continued portfolio disposals.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Rental income was SEK 15,916 million, essentially unchanged from SEK 15,919 million in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Indexation, tenant improvements and occupancy gains supported rental growth, but foreign exchange movements, privatisation and other portfolio sales offset these benefits.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Like-for-like rental income growth remained robust at 4.9%, although it declined from 5.6% in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Real economic occupancy was unchanged at 98.5% for the year and reached 98.7% in the fourth quarter.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Profitability improved through lower operating costs.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Property expenses declined 6.1% to SEK 4,378 million, supported by cost controls, digitalisation, efficiency improvements and the smaller portfolio resulting from disposals.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Consequently, net operating income increased 2.6% to SEK 11,475 million, while the NOI margin rose to 72.1% from 70.3%.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Capital expenditure under the main investment pillars increased to SEK 3,756 million from SEK 3,449 million, particularly reflecting higher maintenance and sustainability spending.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: Tenant improvement investments generated SEK 94 million of additional rental income at an average yield on cost of 10.8%.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: Property values increased by SEK 9,498 million, or 3.0%, compared with 2.6% in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Growth was supported by NOI improvements and value-accretive capital expenditure, as well as strong ownership housing markets, particularly in Denmark.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: The year-end investment property value was SEK 324,429 million, down from SEK 335,422 million because of disposals and currency translation effects.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Privatisation sales reached SEK 10,664 million, with 2,466 units sold at a 28.9% premium to book value.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: Realised gains from property disposals rose to SEK 2,207 million from SEK 1,687 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Profit before tax increased to SEK 16,012 million from SEK 10,403 million, driven by higher property-related earnings, fair value gains and a SEK 3,996 million foreign exchange gain compared with a SEK 2,038 million loss in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: However, the Group recorded a SEK 3,707 million goodwill impairment, primarily because higher discount rates reduced recoverable values for Akelius-related cash-generating units.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: Despite this charge, profit for the year rose to SEK 13,056 million from SEK 7,621 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: The balance sheet strengthened through disposals and debt reduction.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: Net LTV improved to 52.2% from 56.4%, net debt to total assets fell to 48.0% from 51.0%, and ICR increased to 2.0x from 1.9x.
candidate_sentence_map.S21: Heimstaden Bostad completed approximately SEK 59.5 billion of financing transactions, while Heimstaden executed liability-management issues in euros and Swedish kronor.
candidate_sentence_map.S23: A post-year-end Kojamo transaction is expected to reduce Heimstaden’s ownership below 20% and may result in an accounting loss of approximately SEK 3 billion.

evaluation.label: Neutral/Mixed
evaluation.justification: K1, K3, and K5 are PRESENT with core elements covered. K2 is PARTIALLY_PRESENT as it lacks Q4 rental income decrease and LTM margin context. K4, K6, and K7 are MISSING with no coverage of country-specific property value developments, material post-reporting-period events, or sustainability performance metrics. The overall coverage is mixed with major omissions in three HIGH-importance criteria.
